we report a case of peripheral T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma with T-follical helper phenotype that showed secondary cutaneous dissemination as a patient's fourth malignancy.

the clinical features of secondary cutaneous dissemination from peripheral T-cell lymphomas with T-follicle helper phenotype.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this case was diagnosed with a peripheral T-cell lymphomatous infiltration with a follicular helper phenotype as the patient's fourth malignancy, and that the patient had a good prognosis with a 5-year follow-up.
this type of peripheral T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma may disseminate to the skin, which may cause diagnostic confusion.
secondary cutaneous dissemination may occur as a fourth primary malignancy in patients with T-cell lymphoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cutaneous dissemination of T-cell lymphomas can present as a patient's fourth primary malignancy.

the presence of B-cells in a lymphoma expressing a TFH phenotype should not be misinterpreted as evidence for the diagnosis of a T-cell-rich B-cell lymphoma, but rather should be viewed as evidence for the presence of secondary cutaneous dissemination.
peripheral T-cell lymphomas with T-follicle helper cell phenotype should be considered as one of differential diagnosis for patients with erythematous or violaceous nonscaling cutaneous lesions.
